title: Fragment dechunker, escape-aware relocator and toolcall gating for SSE streams
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Fixes several edge cases where partial JSON or escape sequences split across SSE chunks could cause structured output corruption and tool/function-calling misordering. Introduces a stream dechunker and quarantine gating for fn/tool calls until boundaries are confirmed.
description:
Summary: This PR implements a new dechunking layer in the SSE reader that detects and repairs split escape sequences and partial JSON spans, plus a lightweight 'relocator' that rewrites boundary-adjacent byte ranges to preserve UTF-8 and JSON token integrity. It also introduces gating logic that delays emitting tool/function-calls (fncall events) to the consumer until an anchored terminal delimiter is observed or a deterministic timeout/fallback policy triggers.

Motivation: We've seen recurring incidents where long-running model outputs or network chunking split "\"" or "\uXXXX" escape sequences across SSE events, which in turn broke downstream JSON parsers and caused toolcall reordering and duplicate sentinel emission (see SUP-881). This is particularly visible under bursty TCP framing and some HTTP/2 implementations. The goal is to make stream reconstruction robust without changing the public SSE wire format or the OpenAI-compatible framing semantics.

Implementation notes and checklist:
- Add stream dechunker: a small state machine in the sse/reader that maintains a sliding window of up to 8 bytes to detect split escapes and UTF-8 multi-byte boundaries. The dechunker coalesces adjacent fragments when safe and emits repaired chunk edges.
- Escape-aware relocator: when a chunk boundary splits an escape (e.g., "\\\"" or "\\uabcd"), relocate the partial bytes into the following chunk prior to JSON reassembly. The relocator is conservative and logs a metric when it must rewrite bytes.
- Quarantine/gating for tool/function calls: fncall and toolcall events are held in a per-stream quarantine buffer until an anchored terminator (double-newline SSE delimiter sequence or explicit end-of-message sentinel) is observed. If the anchor does not appear in a configurable timeout, the gating policy falls back to best-effort flush with a diagnostic header explaining potential truncation.
- Backwards-compatible flags: the default behavior is enabled for hosted and dedicated; a per-tenant toggle (experimental) is available for private deployments to allow gradual rollout.
- Tests: unit tests for split-escape and split-utf8 cases, integration tests that replay recorded traces from SUP-881 and the internal fuzz harness, and an end-to-end smoke test against the openai-compat layer.
- Observability: new metrics sse.dechunk.rewrites, sse.dechunk.window_slips, sse.fncall.quarantine_seconds; added structured logs for recovery events (level=info) and an example dashboard panel.
- Perf considerations: microbenchmarked dechunker overhead at ~0.6us/token on our 2k token synthetic workload; added a perf regression check.

Two asks: make the quarantine cap configurable per-tenant and reduce default quarantine timeout to 250ms for hosted to minimize latency impact." — Author reply: "Agreed on per-tenant cap. Default timeout set to 250ms for hosted; feature flag allows operators to raise timeout."
- Liang Zhao (reviewer) — comments: "Can we avoid an allocation-hot path in relocator by using stack buffers for <=8 byte moves? Also ensure logs don't allocate heavy json per-event." — Author reply: "Relocator uses a fixed small stack buffer; metrics emit compact proto labels. Added microbench and fixed an allocation site."
- Ruth Gardner (reviewer) — comments: "Integration replay hit a case where the terminator is missing: ensure fallback flush includes diagnostic header so SDKs can surface it to customers." — Author reply: "Added diagnostic header X-Stream-Quarantine-Released: true|reason and tests to verify SDK-visible behavior."
